source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status for Married Persons (combined return); p.6 Mississippi Adjusted Gross Income; p.7 Line 17; FAQ 'At what rate does Mississippi tax my income?'

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 40,000.00 + wages (person 1) 40,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 48,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 1, Married - Combined or Joint Return. Start at federal AGI 80,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 80,000.00. Line 14 standard deduction 4,600.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 12,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 12,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 80,000.00 - 4,600.00 - 12,000.00 = 63,400.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 53,400.00 x 4.4% = 2,349.60; line 4 and line 17 = 2,349.60. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 2,349.60. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 2,350; expected keeps the formula result. On a combined return each column has its own 10,000 band: 31,700.00 in each column, tax 4.4% x 43,400.00 = 1,909.60, which is 440.00 less. Expected follows the projection's one band.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

The 0% band applies to each spouse's taxable income separately on a combined return (Schedule of Tax Computation line 1; FAQ: 'the first $10,000 of each taxpayer's taxable income is exempt'). A projection's schedule runs on the return's total, so married_joint has one 10,000 band. That is exact for a couple with one spouse's income on the return, and too much tax for a couple where both have income. A 20,000 band was not used because it would understate tax for one-income couples, who get one band.
